title: What Changed? — Evidence review
method: Deterministic section anchors and lexical retrieval; no generative AI at runtime.

inputs.before:
# Harbor Desk • Shipping Reference v1
Synthetic demonstration. Not a real company's policy.

## Dispatch window
Submit parcel labels by 3 p.m. local time for same-day dispatch.
The dispatch desk checks the packing list before release.

## Returns
Inspect returned items within 5 business days.
Record the condition and order number in the returns log.

## Archive
Keep the signed dispatch manifest for 90 days.

## Priority service
Example only: a premium customer might receive a replacement in 24 hours.
This illustration is not a service commitment.

## Brand voice
Use the phrase “A little care goes a long way” on the insert.
inputs.after:
# Harbor Desk • Shipping Reference v2

limitations: Text comparison and lexical retrieval, not semantic understanding or compliance certification.
Text unchanged means only the located passage is unchanged; it may not support the checklist instruction.
Section anchors are strongest. Synonyms, renamed headings, cross-references and long multi-topic sections can defeat retrieval.
Example-language detection is a small heuristic, not a complete detector of misleading or nonbinding text.
A changed passage is a review candidate, not an instruction to revise. A person must read the evidence.
